Hi Sara — great to meet your team today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) Summary of recommended approach
- Embedding dimensionality: based on your use-case (semantic search + reranking), we recommend a 1536-dimensional model for best recall. If you need lower memory footprint for large-scale archival search, 768 is viable but expect slightly lower semantic fidelity.
- Similarity: index normalized vectors (L2) and use dot-product at query time — that yields cosine similarity behavior and is faster in many vector DBs that expose dot kernels.
- Batching: for bulk upserts we recommend batching ~128-512 vectors per request depending on your network/worker size; we include an SDK helper that auto-batches and retries on 429s.

2) Migration checklist (from current provider)
- Export: provide a bulk export of vector payloads + ids + original text. CSV/NDJSON with one record per vector is easiest.
- Normalization: if you prefer, normalize at indexing time (recommended) so we can accept raw floats from your exporter and handle L2 on ingest.
- Dedup & mapping: send current doc->id mapping and any canonicalization rules.
- Incremental migration: we typically do a full backfill followed by a cutover window where both systems run; we can support a hybrid routing policy to route 20% of traffic to Redwood for QA before full cutover.

3) SDK & auth
- SDK: our node/python SDKs have bulk upsert and streaming ingestion helpers. I'll attach a short guide and a sample snippet below.
- Auth: we support API keys and mTLS for private deployments. For Dedicated/Private we can also enable per-route keys and IP allowlists.

4) Next steps & owners
- Action: I will share: (a) ACME migration plan (attached), (b) embedding_batching_guide.pdf (attached), and (c) short SDK snippet.
- Technical sync: propose Tue 2027-06-29 10:00 PT for a 45-min migration & architecture session with Ethan and your ML infra team.
- Acceptance criteria: 1) baseline kNN recall parity on your eval set, 2) ingest throughput >= current provider during peak, 3) observation of cost per query within target.

Attachments: acme_migration_plan_v1.pdf, embedding_batching_guide.pdf

Thanks — looping Ethan & Neha for the technical Qs/ops details.

Best,
Marissa

Sara — good Qs, answered inline below. 

1) Storing raw floats: yes, we recommend you keep raw float exports in your cold storage (S3) for debugging and repro — we can accept raw floats and optionally normalize at ingest. Keeping raw floats lets you re-index with different normalization/quantization later.

2) Reranker: for best results we recommend a two-stage pipeline: lexical or vector retrieval followed by a learned reranker. For many customers we return the top-K by cosine (via normalized vectors + dot) and then call a reranker model (LLM or small transformer) for final ranking. If you want to use only vector scores, cosine on normalized vectors works well as a single-stage solution.

3) Quantization: 8-bit (Q8) typically gives a 1-3% drop vs FP16/FP32 on semantic tasks but provides big memory savings. We recommend FP16 for initial migration to minimize regression, then experiment with Q8 for long-term cost. Redwood's runtime supports Q4/Q8 on compatible models and we can recommend quant profiles depending on target recall.

SDK/batching notes:
- The SDK's upsert helper will auto-batch to 256 by default. You can tune batch_size and max_concurrent_requests.
- If you're doing a backfill, use our streaming ingestion mode which keeps a small bounded memory footprint and exposes progress checkpoints.

I've attached the embedding_batching_guide.pdf that covers these tradeoffs. Ethan — can you confirm availability for Tue 29th 10:00 PT and whether you'd like us to kick off a shared test index with 10k sample?

Best,
Marissa
